A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete, readable 16-page paper, including Appendices A-C. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison establish that the research content, equations, figures and tables match.

before.justification: v2 reports original evaluations of ten GUI-agent models on 1,198 simulated examples, plus environment-injection and preference-training experiments (Tables 3-9).

after.justification: v3 retains these original GUI-agent evaluations, environment-injection experiments and preference-training results, including the appendix validation outcome.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the three working patterns, adversarial button rewriting and the DPO preference-training method are identical, including their appendix descriptions.

E1.justification: Both retain the Pop-up box, Search, Recommendation and Chat scenarios, Alpaca-based preference training, and adversarial Pop-up box tests. No dataset or task coverage changes.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical: ten models in Tables 3-7, GPT-4o and GLM-4v in Table 8, and baseline, prompted and DPO-trained Llama configurations in Table 9.

E3.justification: Sample counts, action-matching rules, evaluation metrics, model configurations and working-pattern settings are unchanged. The eight-goal attack protocol and Appendix B training settings also match.

E4.justification: The working-pattern comparisons, adversarial rewriting tests, mitigation experiment and Appendix A shortcut/error and scenario analyses are retained without changes.

E5.justification: Both use the same point-estimate reporting. Neither provides repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals or formal significance tests; no uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: All reported results match, including Tables 3-9 and appendix outcomes. For example, Table 3 retains GPT-4o's Accgold of 74.31 and Accdist of 9.09, and Appendix B.2 retains 96.5% validation accuracy.

T1.justification: The formal problem definitions, action-space formulation, measurement equations and attack formulation in Equations 1-11 are identical. No mathematical definitions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about environmental distractions, GUI-agent vulnerability, perception-related challenges and attack/mitigation contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations of perception versus decision-making, language-centric reasoning and SeeClick shortcuts are unchanged. The Limitations section and Appendix C retain the same qualifications and future directions.

D1.justification: Appendix B preserves the same prompts, generation settings and 3,200-sample LoRA/DPO training recipe. Code-access statements and the code hyperlink are unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion, reference list and Appendix C.2 positioning relative to adversarial attacks are identical. No cited work or substantive positioning changes.

P1.justification: The margin stamp changes from v2 dated 2 July 2025 to v3 dated 5 September 2025. PDF title metadata adds 'LLM', matching the printed title already present in both versions. The paper's prose and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 1-4, Tables 1-9, algorithm and prompt boxes, and page layout are unchanged. Rendered pages 2-16 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp covered under P1.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves the scientific content, evidence, explanations, reproducibility information and limitations of v2, including all appendices. The administrative stamp and title-metadata updates do not meaningfully affect the paper's overall quality.
